title: Orientation, hover, pointer, and resolution features
learningObjectives: Explain orientation, hover, pointer, and resolution features and apply it to responsive components.

understand.concept: Media features can detect orientation, hover capability, pointer accuracy, and display resolution. Examples include orientation:landscape, hover:hover, pointer:fine, and min-resolution. These features describe the environment and input capabilities, not the device's brand.
understand.whyItMatters: Do not assume a touchscreen cannot have a mouse or that every phone is portrait. Combine features carefully and preserve keyboard and touch alternatives.
understand.analogy: These queries ask what kind of display or input capability is available before enhancing the interface.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; media and container queries use formal CSS conditions and sizing references.

explain.narrative: Hover enhancement applies only when the environment reports hover capability and a fine pointer. Landscape orientation adds a border.

examples.explanation: Hover enhancement applies only when the environment reports hover capability and a fine pointer. Landscape orientation adds a border.
examples.expectedOutput: A responsive example that changes based on viewport or container conditions.

practise.guidedTask: Create one rule for fine pointer and hover, and another for orientation. Ensure the control still works without hover.
practise.independentTask: Build a reusable component and test it at different viewport and container sizes, with long labels and text enlargement.
hints: Inspect the actual query condition and container.
Test just below and above thresholds.
Keep content and keyboard order logical.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Orientation, hover, pointer, and resolution features</title></head><body>
<button class='action'>Explore</button><style>.action{padding:1rem}@media(hover:hover) and (pointer:fine){.action:hover{transform:translateY(-2px)}}@media(orientation:landscape){.action{border-inline-start:4px solid #245b48}}</style>
</body></html>
practice.resetCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Orientation, hover, pointer, and resolution features</title></head><body>
<button class='action'>Explore</button><style>.action{padding:1rem}@media(hover:hover) and (pointer:fine){.action:hover{transform:translateY(-2px)}}@media(orientation:landscape){.action{border-inline-start:4px solid #245b48}}</style>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which media feature detects whether the primary pointing device can hover?
questions.explanation: The hover media feature reports whether the primary input mechanism can hover.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable responsive test?
options: Test different widths and content lengths
Test only at one standard phone size
questions.answer: Test different widths and content lengths
questions.explanation: Responsive behaviour depends on actual space and content, not just a device label.
